method: Same host, fresh Python process per full run, five samples per operation/scenario; public async APIs; startup indexing excluded; in-memory storage excludes disk I/O but includes the production persistence snapshot. Loop heartbeat requests 5ms; Windows idle max gaps ranged 16-31ms. Baseline recorded before implementation.
observations: Final executor-future design, worst-scale frequent search: median latency 118.92 -> 119.73ms; maximum heartbeat gap 138.51 -> 46.70ms.
Small median operations remained below 1ms; typical worker scheduling overhead was approximately 0.3-0.4ms.
Vocabulary-heavy maximum-size source create maximum heartbeat gap 111.02 -> 20.72ms; edit tail gap remained 91.03 -> 70.04ms. No universal responsiveness bound is claimed.

An earlier after-run with the same indexing implementation saw an 86ms varied-edit gap; a separate three-repeat limit-only diagnostic saw 21.75ms. These observations illustrate run/scheduler variation and are not substituted for the paired primary measurements.
deferred: _unindex optimization: existing limit-scale public deletion was about 3ms; a direct numbered-chunk lookup saved only about 0.5ms and would rely on an extra contiguity assumption. Original removal retained.

Snapshot/copy-on-write search indexes, process workers, GC policy changes and retrieval algorithm changes: unnecessary complexity for the observed search blocking. Lock-owned search workers retain serialization and cancellation waits for running work.

before.storage: in-memory; serialization included, disk I/O excluded

after.storage: in-memory; serialization included, disk I/O excluded

search_ownership: A context-copied executor future is drained while the existing lock/maintenance admission is held, including repeated/global task cancellation. No independently cancellable child task wraps the worker. Regression detects early lock release in the child-task/to_thread design.
